items.title: 2.7 Equations of Tangent and Normal Lines to a Curve (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 44-45: 2.7 tangent line, Need to Know! (vertical tangent), normal line, Note box, Example 10 (y = sec x at x = pi/4)

blocks.text: Ab tak is unit mein humne derivative nikalna seekha: trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential aur logarithmic functions ke derivatives. Lekin derivative ka faida kya hai? Is section mein uska pehla bara istemal dekhte hain. Derivative \(f'(x_0)\) asal mein curve ka slope (dhalwan, yani curve kitna tez upar ya neeche ja raha hai) hai us point par jahan \(x = x_0\). Aur Class XI se aap jaante hain ke agar ek point aur slope maloom ho to line ki equation point-slope form se foran likhi ja sakti hai. Bas yahi is sabaq ka poora khel hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text:
Kitab ki definition: maan lijiye \(x_0\) function \(f(x)\) ke domain mein ek point hai. Curve \(y = f(x)\) ki tangent line point \((x_0, f(x_0))\) par woh line hai jis ki equation yeh hai:
\[y - y_0 = m(x - x_0)\]
jahan \(m = f'(x_0) = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x = x_0}\), basharte ke \(f'(x_0)\) exist kare (yani derivative maujood ho).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh equation kyun? Tangent line (chhoone wali line) curve ko point \((x_0, y_0)\) par chhooti hai aur wahan bilkul curve ki direction mein chalti hai. Curve ki direction yani slope derivative hi naapta hai. Is liye tangent ka slope \(m = f'(x_0)\) hai, aur point-slope form se line ban jati hai.
Yahan \(y_0 = f(x_0)\) hai: \(y_0\) hamesha curve ki equation mein \(x_0\) rakh kar nikalte hain, derivative mein rakh kar nahi.
Nishaan \(\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x = x_0}\) ka matlab hai: "pehle \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikalo, phir us mein \(x = x_0\) rakho". Tarteeb ulti kabhi na karein.

blocks.title: Need to Know!
blocks.text: Vertical Tangent: agar \(x = x_0\) par \(m\) ki value \(\infty\) ya \(-\infty\) ho, to line \(x = x_0\) curve \(y = f(x)\) ki tangent hoti hai; ise vertical tangent (khari tangent) kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Amal mein \(m = \pm\infty\) kaise pehchanein? \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ko ek fraction ki shakal mein likhiye. Jahan denominator zero ho aur numerator zero na ho, wahan slope "be-hadd bara" ho jata hai, yani tangent khari (vertical) hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal (kitab se nahi): circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\) par \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{y}\). Point \((5, 0)\) par denominator \(y = 0\) hai, is liye wahan tangent vertical line \(x = 5\) hai. Circle ki tasveer zehan mein laiye: daayen kinare par circle bilkul seedha upar neeche ja raha hota hai.
Ulti soorat: jahan \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) ho, wahan tangent leti hui (horizontal) hoti hai: \(y = y_0\).
Kitab ki definition: curve \(y = f(x)\) ke point \((x_0, f(x_0))\) se guzarne wali woh line jo tangent line par perpendicular (90 degree par khari) ho, curve \(y = f(x)\) ki normal line kehlati hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kisi point par curve ki tangent line ka slope hi us point par curve ka slope kehlata hai.

Agar \(m = f'(x_0)\) zero na ho, to normal line ki equation yeh hai:
\[y - y_0 = -\frac{1}{m}(x - x_0)\]
aur agar \(m = f'(x_0) = 0\) ho, to normal line ki equation \(x = x_0\) hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(-\frac{1}{m}\) kahan se aaya? Class XI ka rule yaad kijiye: do perpendicular lines (jo vertical na hon) ke slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai. Tangent ka slope \(m\) hai, to normal ka slope \(m_2\) aisa hoga ke \(m \cdot m_2 = -1\), yani \(m_2 = -\frac{1}{m}\). Yaad karne ka aasan jumla: "slope ko ulta karo aur sign badal do". Misaal: tangent ka slope 2 ho to normal ka \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
Agar tangent leti hui ho (\(m = 0\)) to normal khara hoga: \(x = x_0\). Aur agar tangent khari (vertical) ho to normal leta hua hoga: \(y = y_0\). Yahan formula \(-\frac{1}{m}\) kaam nahi karta kyunke zero se divide nahi kar sakte, is liye yeh do soortein alag yaad rakhiye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar kisi point par tangent ka slope \(-3\) ho to normal ka slope kya hoga?
Jawab: \(-\frac{1}{-3} = \frac{1}{3}\). Check: \((-3) \times \frac{1}{3} = -1\), yani dono perpendicular hain.
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yeh teeno qadam chala kar dekhte hain.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: Find the equations of the tangent and normal to the curve \(y = \sec x\) at the point where \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\).
steps:
Diya gaya: curve \(y = \sec x\) aur woh point jahan \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\).
Maloom karna: us point par tangent aur normal dono ki equations.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke line ke liye do cheezein chahiye: ek point aur ek slope. Point curve ki equation se milega, aur slope derivative se. \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\) par derivative tangent ka slope \(m\) dega, aur normal ka slope \(-\frac{1}{m}\) hoga. Phir dono lines point-slope form se.

Step 1: Derivative nikalein
\[y = \sec x \quad \text{...(1)}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec x\tan x\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sec x) = \sec x\tan x\) un chhe standard derivatives mein se hai jo humne 2.2 mein parhe. Abhi \(x\) ki value nahi rakhi, pehle derivative poora kiya.

Step 2: Tangent ka slope
\[m = \sec\dfrac{\pi}{4}\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[= \sqrt{2}\cdot 1 = \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) hai, to us ka ulta \(\sec\frac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}\); aur \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\). Yani \(45^\circ\) wale angle ki values. Ab humare paas slope aa gaya.

Step 3: Curve par point
(1) mein \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\) rakhein:
\[y = \sec\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}\]
\[(x_0, y_0) = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \sqrt{2}\right)\]
Kyun: tangent aur normal dono isi point se guzarti hain. \(y_0\) curve ki equation (1) se aata hai, derivative se nahi.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(y_0\) aur \(m\) dono \(\sqrt{2}\) hain, yeh sirf ittefaq hai; aam tor par yeh alag hote hain.

Step 4: Tangent ki equation
\[y - \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[y - \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}x - \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{2}}{4}\]
\[4y - 4\sqrt{2} = 4\sqrt{2}x - \pi\sqrt{2}\]
\[4\sqrt{2}x - 4y + 4\sqrt{2} - \pi\sqrt{2} = 0\]
Kyun: point-slope form \(y - y_0 = m(x - x_0)\) mein values rakhin. Phir bracket khola, poori equation ko 4 se multiply kiya taa ke fraction khatam ho jaye, aur sab terms ek taraf le aaye.

Step 5: Normal ki equation
Normal ka slope \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) hai:
\[y - \sqrt{2} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]
Dono taraf \(4\sqrt{2}\) se multiply karein:
\[4\sqrt{2}y - 8 = -4x + \pi\]
\[4x + 4\sqrt{2}y - 8 - \pi = 0\]
Kyun: \(4\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2} = 4 \times 2 = 8\), aur right side par \(4\sqrt{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 4\), to \(-4\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -4x + \pi\). Phir sab ek taraf.
Dhyan dein: multiply karte waqt har term ko multiply karna hai. \(x\) ka coefficient 4 hai, 1 nahi (kitab yahan ghalti karti hai, neeche dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
Point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}, \sqrt{2}\right)\) tangent mein rakhein:
\[\pi\sqrt{2} - 4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2} - \pi\sqrt{2} = 0\]
aur normal mein:
\[\pi + 8 - 8 - \pi = 0\]
Dono lines point se guzarti hain. Slopes: tangent \(\sqrt{2}\), normal \(-\frac{4}{4\sqrt{2}} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\); product \(-1\), yani dono waqai perpendicular hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 10 mein kitab normal ki equation \(x + 4\sqrt{2}y - 8 - \pi = 0\) likhti hai, jo ghalat hai. \(y - \sqrt{2} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) ko \(4\sqrt{2}\) se multiply karein to \(4\sqrt{2}y - 8 = -4x + \pi\) banta hai, is liye sahi equation \(4x + 4\sqrt{2}y - 8 - \pi = 0\) hai. Kitab wali line to point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}, \sqrt{2}\right)\) se guzarti bhi nahi: rakhne par 0 ki bajaye \(-\frac{3\pi}{4}\) aata hai. Sabaq: aakhri equation mein point rakh kar zaroor check kijiye.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Curve \(y = x^{2}\) par point \((1, 1)\) par tangent aur normal (yeh misaal hamari hai, kitab ki nahi).
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\), to \(m = 2\).
Tangent: \(y - 1 = 2(x - 1)\), yani \(y = 2x - 1\).
Normal: slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\), \(y - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 1)\), yani \(x + 2y - 3 = 0\).
Check: \((1, 1)\) dono mein: \(2 - 1 = 1\) aur \(1 + 2 - 3 = 0\). Bilkul theek.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Point \(x_0\) par curve ka slope = tangent ka slope = \(f'(x_0)\).
2. Tangent: \(y - y_0 = m(x - x_0)\), jahan \(y_0 = f(x_0)\) curve se nikalta hai.
3. Normal: \(y - y_0 = -\frac{1}{m}(x - x_0)\) jab \(m \ne 0\); perpendicular lines ke slopes ka product \(-1\).
4. \(m = 0\): tangent \(y = y_0\) (leti hui), normal \(x = x_0\) (khari).
5. \(m = \pm\infty\) (\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ka denominator zero): tangent \(x = x_0\) (vertical tangent), normal \(y = y_0\).
6. Aakhir mein point ko dono equations mein rakh kar tasdeeq zaroor karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Differentiate karne se pehle hi \(x_0\) rakh dena: \(\sec\frac{\pi}{4}\) ek constant hai aur us ka derivative 0 aayega, jo bilkul ghalat hai. Pehle derivative, phir value.
2. Normal ke liye \(-\frac{1}{m}\) ki jagah \(m\) hi le lena, ya minus sign bhool jana.
3. \(y_0\) curve se nikalne ki bajaye slope ki value ko \(y_0\) samajh lena.
4. Fraction khatam karte waqt sirf kuch terms ko multiply karna (bilkul yahi ghalti kitab ke Example 10 ke normal mein chhap gayi hai).
